findings.evidence: `ProC.lean` lines 123–403 correspond directly to `MaximalProP.lean` lines 117–437: e.g. `mem_proCKernel_iff`/`mem_proPKernel_iff`, `map_proCKernel_eq`/`map_proPKernel_eq`, `proCCompletion.map`/`maximalProPQuotient.map`, the compactness proofs at lines 208/235, lifts at lines 297/328, and idempotence at lines 364/396. `FiniteGroupClass.lean` lines 196, 211, 223 likewise parallel `PGroup.lean` lines 50, 128, 144.
findings.fix: Refactor the pro-p development and its consumers onto the generic finite-group-class construction, retaining only genuinely pro-p-specific results rather than two independently maintained implementations.
findings.issue: The new pro-C kernel/completion API is a near-verbatim parallel implementation of the existing pro-p API, including kernel membership, functoriality, compactness, universal property, and idempotence; the analogous duplication also occurs between `MemFinite.prod`/`quotient_inf`/`quotient_comap` and the existing `IsPGroup` lemmas.

summary: The generic pro-C development leaves a large specialized pro-p implementation duplicated instead of making the generic construction canonical.
